beats.headline: Passing a String variable printed Object!
beats.subline: Method overloading traps even experienced developers.
beats.narration: You pass a String object into an overloaded method, but Java executes the Object signature instead. Let's uncover why compile time overloading tricks your code while run time overriding dynamic dispatch saves it.

beats.title: Overloading vs. Overriding

top.label: Method Overloading
points: Resolved by javac at compile time

bottom.label: Method Overriding
bottom.code:
PaymentProcessor p = new CardProcessor();
p.charge(49.99); // Executes CardProcessor!
points: Resolved at runtime on heap object

beats.narration: Method overloading binds statically at compile time using the reference declared type. So passing a String stored in an Object variable hits Object check. Overriding dynamically dispatches at runtime based on the actual object on the heap.

beats.title: Dynamic Dispatch in Action

steps.explanation: Defines supertype contract so callers avoid monolithic if-else type checks.
Subclass overrides implementation; runtime heap type determines which charge executes.

beats.narration: Instead of writing fragile if else chains checking item types, define a supertype contract. Subclasses override charge, allowing callers to trigger concrete behavior without knowing the exact runtime subtype in advance.

beats.title: Non-Overridable Members

steps.explanation: Static methods, private methods, and fields do not participate in dynamic dispatch.
Final methods cannot be overridden; javac resolves them with static binding.

beats.narration: Be careful: static methods, private methods, constructors, and fields never participate in dynamic dispatch. Calling a static method resolves strictly against the reference type at compile time.

beats.title: Part 1 Locked In
takeaways: Overloading binds statically using declared argument types
Overriding dispatches dynamically based on heap object
Static methods and fields never dynamic dispatch

beats.headline: How does the JVM find method code in 1 nanosecond?
beats.subline: HotSpot vtables and JIT inline caching eliminate dispatch overhead.
beats.narration: When your code calls a virtual method on an interface reference, how does the JVM instantly pinpoint the correct machine code instruction? Let's trace HotSpot's internal vtables and JIT inline caching.

beats.title: HotSpot vtable Method Lookup
beats.subtitle: Tracing invokevirtual from Stack to Machine Code

nodes.label: Thread Stack Ref
nodes.detail: Processor ref points to object address on heap

nodes.label: Heap Object Header
nodes.detail: Reads Klass pointer inside object header

nodes.label: Metaspace vtable
nodes.detail: Direct O(1) slot index lookup in class metadata

nodes.label: JIT Code Cache
nodes.detail: Jumps directly to compiled native machine code

beats.narration: During invokevirtual calls, HotSpot follows the reference to the heap object, reads its class metadata pointer in Metaspace, inspects the vtable at a fixed offset, and jumps directly to compiled machine code.

beats.title: vtable vs. itable Lookup

top.label: vtable (invokevirtual)
points: Class hierarchy shares fixed method slots

bottom.label: itable (invokeinterface)
points: Classes implement interfaces in any order

beats.narration: Class methods use vtables where subclasses share identical slot indices for instant array reads. Interface methods use itables because unrelated classes implement interfaces in different order, requiring dynamic table resolution.

beats.title: JIT Inline Caching States
beats.subtitle: How JIT bypasses vtable lookup completely

nodes.label: Monomorphic Call Site
nodes.detail: Only 1 concrete class seen; JIT inlines code directly

nodes.label: Bimorphic Call Site
nodes.detail: 2 concrete classes seen; JIT emits fast 2-way branch

nodes.label: Megamorphic Call Site
nodes.detail: 3+ classes seen; falls back to vtable or itable lookup

beats.narration: HotSpot JIT profiles call sites at runtime. Monomorphic sites seeing only one class get fully inlined. Bimorphic sites use a fast two-way check. Only megamorphic sites seeing three or more classes pay for vtable lookup.

beats.title: Part 2 Locked In
takeaways: invokevirtual uses O(1) vtable slot indexing
invokeinterface resolves dynamic offsets via itable
JIT inline caching inlines monomorphic call sites

beats.headline: ClassCastException in production?
beats.subline: Explicit downcasting without checks is a ticking time bomb.
beats.narration: Casting supertype references to subtypes looks harmless until an unexpected object hits your pipeline and crashes production with a ClassCastException. Let's fix type safety once and for all.

beats.title: Upcasting vs. Downcasting Safety
beats.subtitle: Implicit supertype vs. Explicit subtype conversion

nodes.label: Subtype Object (Dog)
nodes.detail: Concrete instance allocated on JVM heap

nodes.label: Upcasting (Implicit)
nodes.detail: Assign to Animal supertype variable (always safe)

nodes.label: Downcasting (Explicit)
nodes.detail: (Dog) pet required by compiler; unsafe without check

nodes.label: ClassCastException
nodes.detail: JVM throws runtime error if actual object is Cat

beats.narration: Upcasting to a supertype variable happens automatically because every subclass satisfies the base contract. Downcasting back requires an explicit cast because the compiler cannot guarantee the heap object true identity at runtime.

beats.title: Classic instanceof Guard Rules

steps.explanation: null instanceof Anything always returns false—no NPE risk!
Manual cast required before Java 16 pattern matching.

beats.narration: The instanceof operator checks runtime compatibility. Notice that null instanceof anything is always false, avoiding NullPointerExceptions. But notice how pre-Java 16 code repeats the type name three times.

beats.title: Compiler Checks vs. Runtime Crashes
beats.caption: What compiles versus what fails at runtime

lines.text: # 1. Unrelated class check is caught at compile time!
error: inconvertible types: String cannot be converted to Integer
Exception in thread main java.lang.ClassCastException: Cat cannot be cast to Dog

beats.narration: The compiler blocks casting unrelated types like String to Integer. But when casting supertypes like Animal to Dog, invalid heap objects compile cleanly and crash at runtime with a ClassCastException.

beats.title: Part 3 Locked In
takeaways: Upcasting is implicit and completely safe
Downcasting requires runtime checks to avoid ClassCastException
null instanceof Target evaluates safely to false

beats.headline: Stop repeating type names three times!
beats.subline: Java 16 pattern matching and Java 21 switch eliminate boilerplate casts.
beats.narration: Writing instanceof, declaring a variable, and casting on the next line is redundant and error-prone. Modern Java makes pattern matching clean, safe, and scoped with flow precision.

beats.title: Classic vs. Pattern Matching instanceof

top.label: Pre-Java 16 (Redundant)

beats.narration: Java 16 pattern matching combines type checking, variable declaration, and casting into a single atomic expression. If animal matches Dog, pattern variable dog is bound and ready to use immediately.

beats.title: Flow Scoping & Guard Clauses

steps.explanation: dog is in scope on the right side of && because left side is guaranteed true.
dog stays in scope after early return because execution only continues when matched.

beats.narration: Pattern variables use flow scoping. In an AND check, dog is in scope on the right side. In a negated early return guard, dog stays in scope for the rest of the method.

beats.title: Java 21 Pattern Matching switch

steps.explanation: Refines pattern with extra boolean condition before matching.
Explicit null handling eliminates NullPointerException inside switch expressions.

beats.narration: Java 21 switch expressions bring type patterns, extra when guards, and explicit case null branches together. When paired with sealed interfaces, the compiler guarantees exhaustive branch coverage without a default case.
